channel.title: The Lowndes Signal - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Lowndes Signal (lowndessignal.com)

item.title: Students explore jobs at career expo
item.description: Lowndes County students met with 32 employers, colleges, military and local leaders at The Calhoun School’s Career Compass expo to explore real-world job paths.

item.title: Swing for fences: Vote now
item.description: Vote for Lowndes County Athlete of the Week: support nominees Timarion Williams, Whit Holley and Ameriyah Hartley in online voting open hourly through Tuesday at noon.

item.title: Memories from the Opelika Hospital
item.description: An Alabama pastor recalls learning of Reagan’s 1981 shooting at an Opelika hospital and an unexpected $20 bill that shaped his reflections on suffering, gratitude and God’s gifts.

item.title: Time with God sparks change
item.description: Pastor Dunford Cole reflects on how regular time with God visibly transforms believers — from renewed minds to changed daily lives — and why true encounters with God always leave a lasting mark.

item.title: The fine print of ambition
item.description: An advice column on the fine line between healthy ambition and being “always available,” urging workers to question whether nonstop hustle is worth the personal cost.

item.title: Specialty crop grant applications open
item.description: Alabama agriculture department is accepting applications for USDA specialty crop block grants, offering $5,000–$40,000 for eligible commodity groups, organizations and institutions.

item.title: Fields & Forests plants millionth tree
item.description: Fields & Forests marks its millionth tree in Lowndes County, helping small landowners turn underused fields into income-producing forests and carbon credits.

item.title: Who should use AI?
item.description: Author argues AI suits research and high‑risk professions, but says creative writers should not rely on it, warning it can erase personal voice and deny use of God‑given talent.

item.title: Young learners excel in spelling bee
item.description: Lowndes County students in grades 2 – 8 showcased their spelling skills Feb. 25, with Hayneville and Central learners earning top spots in the district spelling bee.

item.title: Central freshman sinks athlete contest win
item.description: Central High freshman Timarion Williams wins Lowndes County Athlete of the Week, earning 52% of 225 votes in round 24 of the 2025-26 sports season.
